import os
import json
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import simpledialog, messagebox, colorchooser
from PIL import Image, ImageTk
import cv2
import threading
import time
from src.managers.model_manager import ModelManager
from src.adapters.yolo_adapter import YOLOAdapter

class VideoGUI:
    def __init__(self, project):
        self.project = project
        self.model_manager = ModelManager()
        
        # Initialize Adapters (Reuse Vision adapters for frame-by-frame)
        self.adapters = {
            "yolo": YOLOAdapter(project),
        }
        self.active_adapter = self.adapters["yolo"]

        self.master = tk.Tk()
        self.master.title(f"NeuroLoop (Video) - {self.project.project_name}")

        # Video Data Setup
        # For video projects, we expect the image_dir to contain video files
        self.data_dir = self.project.image_dir_source # Reusing this config key
        self.supported_extensions = (".mp4", ".avi", ".mov", ".mkv")
            
        self.video_files = sorted(
            [
                f
                for f in os.listdir(self.data_dir)
                if f.lower().endswith(self.supported_extensions)
            ]
        )
        
        if not self.video_files:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "No video files found in the project directory.")
            self.master.destroy()
            return

        self.current_video_index = 0
        self.cap = None
        self.total_frames = 0
        self.current_frame_idx = 0
        self.fps = 30
        self.is_playing = False
        
        # Load session state
        # structure: annotations[video_filename][frame_idx] = { objects: ... }
        self.user_annotations = self.project.session.get("annotations", {})
        
        # UI State
        self.active_tool = "bbox" 
        self.start_x, self.start_y, self.current_shape, self.selected_label = None, None, None, None
        self.scale = 1.0
        self.tkimg = None
        self.frame_image = None # PIL Image of current frame

        self.label_file = os.path.join(self.project.dataset_dir, "labels.json")
        self.label_list, self.label_colors = self.load_label_list()

        self._setup_ui()
        self.master.protocol("WM_DELETE_WINDOW", self.on_closing)

        self.load_video(self.video_files[0])

    def on_closing(self):
        if self.cap: self.cap.release()
        self.save_session()
        self.master.destroy()

    def save_session(self):
        print(f"Saving session...")
        self.project.save_session(self.user_annotations, self.current_video_index, 0)
        self.save_label_list()

    def load_video(self, filename):
        if self.cap: self.cap.release()
        path = os.path.join(self.data_dir, filename)
        self.cap = cv2.VideoCapture(path)
        self.total_frames = int(self.cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
        self.fps = self.cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS) or 30
        self.current_frame_idx = 0
        
        self.master.title(f"NeuroLoop (Video) - {filename}")
        self.timeline.config(to=self.total_frames - 1)
        self.seek_frame(0)

    def seek_frame(self, frame_idx):
        if not self.cap: return
        self.cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, frame_idx)
        ret, frame = self.cap.read()
        if ret:
            self.current_frame_idx = frame_idx
            # Convert BGR to RGB
            cv2_im = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
            self.frame_image = Image.fromarray(cv2_im)
            self.show_scaled_image()
            self.timeline.set(frame_idx)
            self.update_stats()
        else:
            print("Error reading frame.")

    def _setup_ui(self):
        self.main_frame = tk.Frame(self.master)
        self.main_frame.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)

        # Canvas
        self.canvas_frame = tk.Frame(self.main_frame)
        self.canvas_frame.pack(side=tk.LEFT, fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
        self.canvas = tk.Canvas(self.canvas_frame, cursor="cross", bg="#333")
        self.canvas.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)

        # Timeline Slider
        self.timeline_frame = tk.Frame(self.master)
        self.timeline_frame.pack(side=tk.BOTTOM, fill=tk.X, padx=10, pady=5)
        self.timeline = tk.Scale(self.timeline_frame, from_=0, to=100, orient=tk.HORIZONTAL, command=self.on_slider_move)
        self.timeline.pack(fill=tk.X)
        
        # Controls
        self.controls_frame = tk.Frame(self.master)
        self.controls_frame.pack(side=tk.BOTTOM, fill=tk.X, pady=5)
        tk.Button(self.controls_frame, text="<<", command=lambda: self.seek_relative(-30)).pack(side=tk.LEFT)
        tk.Button(self.controls_frame, text="<", command=lambda: self.seek_relative(-1)).pack(side=tk.LEFT)
        self.play_btn = tk.Button(self.controls_frame, text="Play", command=self.toggle_play)
        self.play_btn.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=20)
        tk.Button(self.controls_frame, text=">", command=lambda: self.seek_relative(1)).pack(side=tk.LEFT)
        tk.Button(self.controls_frame, text=">>", command=lambda: self.seek_relative(30)).pack(side=tk.LEFT)

        # Right Panel
        self.control_panel = tk.Frame(self.main_frame, padx=10, pady=10)
        self.control_panel.pack(side=tk.RIGHT, fill=tk.Y)
        self._setup_tools_panel()
        self._setup_annotation_panel()

        # Canvas Bindings
        self.canvas.bind("<ButtonPress-1>", self.on_button_press)
        self.canvas.bind("<B1-Motion>", self.on_move_press)
        self.canvas.bind("<ButtonRelease-1>", self.on_button_release)
        self.master.bind("<space>", self.toggle_play)

        self.stats_label = tk.Label(self.master, text="", anchor="w")
        self.stats_label.pack(side=tk.BOTTOM, fill=tk.X)

    def _setup_tools_panel(self):
        tools_frame = tk.LabelFrame(self.control_panel, text="Tools", padx=5, pady=5)
        tools_frame.pack(fill=tk.X, pady=5)
        self.tool_var = tk.StringVar(value="bbox")
        tk.Radiobutton(tools_frame, text="Bounding Box", variable=self.tool_var, value="bbox", command=lambda: setattr(self, 'active_tool', 'bbox')).pack(anchor="w")

    def _setup_annotation_panel(self):
        anno_frame = tk.LabelFrame(self.control_panel, text="Annotations", padx=5, pady=5)
        anno_frame.pack(fill=tk.X, pady=5)

        tk.Label(anno_frame, text="Labels:").pack(anchor="w")
        self.label_listbox = tk.Listbox(anno_frame, height=8, exportselection=False)
        self.label_listbox.pack(fill=tk.X)
        self.label_listbox.bind("<<ListboxSelect>>", self.on_label_select)
        self.populate_label_listbox()
        
        self.label_entry = tk.Entry(anno_frame)
        self.label_entry.pack(fill=tk.X)
        tk.Button(anno_frame, text="Add Label", command=self.add_label).pack(fill=tk.X)

    # --- Video Logic ---
    def on_slider_move(self, val):
        # Only seek if not playing to avoid conflict, or simple debounce
        if not self.is_playing:
            self.seek_frame(int(val))

    def seek_relative(self, delta):
        new_idx = max(0, min(self.total_frames-1, self.current_frame_idx + delta))
        self.seek_frame(new_idx)

    def toggle_play(self, event=None):
        self.is_playing = not self.is_playing
        self.play_btn.config(text="Pause" if self.is_playing else "Play")
        if self.is_playing:
            threading.Thread(target=self.play_loop, daemon=True).start()

    def play_loop(self):
        while self.is_playing and self.current_frame_idx < self.total_frames - 1:
            start_time = time.time()
            self.current_frame_idx += 1
            
            # Update UI in main thread
            # We can't call canvas update from thread easily without slight risk, 
            # but reading frame is IO bound. 
            # Ideally use master.after.
            self.master.after_idle(lambda: self.timeline.set(self.current_frame_idx))
            self.master.after_idle(lambda idx=self.current_frame_idx: self.seek_frame(idx))
            
            elapsed = time.time() - start_time
            delay = max(0.001, (1.0/self.fps) - elapsed)
            time.sleep(delay)
        
        if self.current_frame_idx >= self.total_frames - 1:
            self.is_playing = False
            self.play_btn.config(text="Play")

    # --- Display & Annotation ---
    def show_scaled_image(self):
        if not self.frame_image: return
        w, h = self.frame_image.size
        # Simple scale to fit if needed, or keep 1.0
        new_size = (int(w * self.scale), int(h * self.scale))
        resized = self.frame_image.resize(new_size, Image.LANCZOS)
        self.tkimg = ImageTk.PhotoImage(resized)
        self.canvas.delete("all")
        self.canvas.create_image(0, 0, anchor="nw", image=self.tkimg)
        self.canvas.config(scrollregion=self.canvas.bbox(tk.ALL))
        self.redraw_annotations()

    def redraw_annotations(self):
        vid_key = self.video_files[self.current_video_index]
        frame_key = str(self.current_frame_idx)
        
        # Structure: annotations -> filename -> frame_idx_str -> objects
        # Note: JSON keys are strings
        anns = self.user_annotations.get(vid_key, {}).get(frame_key, {}).get("objects", [])
        
        for ann in anns:
            color = self.label_colors.get(ann["label"], "yellow")
            if ann["type"] == "bbox":
                x1, y1, x2, y2 = [p * self.scale for p in ann["points"]]
                self.canvas.create_rectangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, outline=color, width=2, tags="annotation")
                self.canvas.create_text(x1, y1, text=ann["label"], anchor="sw", fill=color, tags="annotation")

    # --- Drawing ---
    def on_button_press(self, event):
        if not self.selected_label: return
        self.start_x = self.canvas.canvasx(event.x)
        self.start_y = self.canvas.canvasy(event.y)
        self.current_shape = self.canvas.create_rectangle(self.start_x, self.start_y, self.start_x, self.start_y, outline="cyan")

    def on_move_press(self, event):
        if self.current_shape:
            cur_x, cur_y = self.canvas.canvasx(event.x), self.canvas.canvasy(event.y)
            self.canvas.coords(self.current_shape, self.start_x, self.start_y, cur_x, cur_y)

    def on_button_release(self, event):
        if self.current_shape:
            x1, y1, x2, y2 = self.canvas.coords(self.current_shape)
            self.canvas.delete(self.current_shape)
            self.current_shape = None
            
            # Save annotation
            vid_key = self.video_files[self.current_video_index]
            frame_key = str(self.current_frame_idx)
            
            self.user_annotations.setdefault(vid_key, {})
            self.user_annotations[vid_key].setdefault(frame_key, {"objects": []})
            
            ann = {
                "type": "bbox",
                "label": self.selected_label,
                "points": [int(min(x1, x2) / self.scale), int(min(y1, y2) / self.scale), int(max(x1, x2) / self.scale), int(max(y1, y2) / self.scale)]
            }
            self.user_annotations[vid_key][frame_key]["objects"].append(ann)
            self.redraw_annotations()

    # --- Labels ---
    def load_label_list(self):
        if os.path.exists(self.label_file):
            with open(self.label_file, "r") as f:
                d = json.load(f)
                return d.get("labels", []), d.get("colors", {})
        return [], {}

    def save_label_list(self):
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.label_file), exist_ok=True)
        with open(self.label_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"labels": self.label_list, "colors": self.label_colors}, f)

    def populate_label_listbox(self):
        self.label_listbox.delete(0, tk.END)
        for l in self.label_list: self.label_listbox.insert(tk.END, l)

    def add_label(self):
        l = self.label_entry.get().strip()
        if l and l not in self.label_list:
            self.label_list.append(l)
            self.label_colors[l] = "red"
            self.populate_label_listbox()

    def on_label_select(self, event):
        sel = self.label_listbox.curselection()
        if sel: self.selected_label = self.label_list[sel[0]]

    def update_stats(self):
        self.stats_label.config(text=f"Frame: {self.current_frame_idx}/{self.total_frames} | Time: {self.current_frame_idx/self.fps:.2f}s")

response.output:
# NeuroLoop: Multimodal HITL Platform

**NeuroLoop** is a local, privacy-first, desktop application designed to accelerate the creation of custom AI models for **Vision** (Object Detection/Segmentation) and **Audio** (Sound Event Detection).

It replaces the standard "Label -> Train" waterfall with a **Reinforcement Cycle**:
1.  **Bootstrap:** Use Foundation Models (Florence-2, SAM 2, CLAP) to auto-label data.
2.  **Interact:** Human corrects only the edge cases using a dedicated GUI.
3.  **Reinforce:** Background processes retrain the model on the corrected data.
4.  **Loop:** The model gets smarter every few clicks.

For detailed architecture and developer documentation, please see [NeuroLoop.md](NeuroLoop.md).

## Features

- **Split Scope Interfaces:**
    - **Vision Scope:** Dedicated GUI for Images/Video with Bounding Box, Polygon tools, and Synthetic Data Generation.
    - **Audio Scope:** Dedicated GUI for Waveform/Spectrogram analysis and Sound Event Detection.
- **Foundation Model Integration:** 
    - **Vision:** YOLO11, Florence-2 (Auto-boxing), SAM 2 (Auto-masking).
    - **Audio:** CLAP (Zero-shot detection).
- **Human-in-the-Loop Workflow:**
    - Load a pre-trained model to get initial predictions.
    - Correct predictions in the GUI.
    - Automatic background retraining after N corrections (Reinforcement Training).

## Installation

1.  **Clone the repository**.
2.  **Create and activate a virtual environment** (e.g., `uv`, `venv`).
3.  **Install dependencies:**
    ```bash
    uv pip install -r requirements.txt
    # or
    pip install -r requirements.txt
    ```

## Usage

Run the main entry point:
```bash
python -m src.main
```
You will be prompted to select or create a project. Based on the project type (Vision or Audio), the appropriate GUI will launch.

## Changelog

See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for a list of recent changes and features.

import os
import json
import torch
import numpy as np
import librosa
from src.adapters.base_adapter import BaseAdapter

# Try to import Transformers CLAP
try:
    from transformers import ClapModel, ClapProcessor
    TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = False

try:
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    WHISPER_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    WHISPER_AVAILABLE = False

class AudioAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    def __init__(self, project):
        super().__init__(project)
        self.project = project
        self.model = None
        self.processor = None
        self.whisper_model = None
        self.device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
        self.model_id = "laion/clap-htsat-unfused" # Standard HF model

    @property
    def name(self):
        return "clap"

    def load(self):
        if not TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE:
            print("Error: 'transformers' library not found or missing CLAP support.")
            return

        print(f"Loading CLAP ({self.model_id}) on {self.device}...")
        try:
            self.model = ClapModel.from_pretrained(self.model_id).to(self.device)
            self.processor = ClapProcessor.from_pretrained(self.model_id)
            print("CLAP loaded successfully.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error loading CLAP: {e}")

    def load_whisper(self):
        if not WHISPER_AVAILABLE:
            print("Error: 'faster-whisper' library not found.")
            return None
        
        if self.whisper_model is None:
            print(f"Loading Faster-Whisper (tiny) on {self.device}...")
            # Compute type: float16 on GPU, int8 on CPU usually
            compute_type = "float16" if self.device == "cuda" else "int8"
            try:
                self.whisper_model = WhisperModel("tiny", device=self.device, compute_type=compute_type)
                print("Faster-Whisper loaded.")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error loading Whisper: {e}")
        return self.whisper_model

    def predict(self, audio_path, **kwargs):
        """
        Predicts sound events.
        Kwargs:
            classes (list): List of text labels for zero-shot classification.
        """
        if self.model is None:
            self.load()
            if self.model is None: return []

        classes = kwargs.get("classes", [])
        if not classes:
            print("Warning: No classes provided for Audio prediction. Returning empty.")
            return []

        try:
            # Load audio at 48k as per CLAP standard usually
            audio_array, sr = librosa.load(audio_path, sr=48000)
            
            chunk_duration = 5.0 # seconds
            chunk_samples = int(chunk_duration * 48000)
            
            predictions = []
            
            # Prepare text inputs once
            text_inputs = self.processor(text=classes, return_tensors="pt", padding=True).to(self.device)
            
            for i in range(0, len(audio_array), chunk_samples):
                chunk = audio_array[i:i+chunk_samples]
                if len(chunk) < 1000: break # Skip tiny chunks
                
                # Processor handles resampling if needed, but we already loaded at 48k
                audio_inputs = self.processor(audios=chunk, sampling_rate=48000, return_tensors="pt").to(self.device)
                
                with torch.no_grad():
                    outputs = self.model(**text_inputs, **audio_inputs)
                
                # outputs.logits_per_audio: (batch_size, num_text)
                probs = outputs.logits_per_audio.softmax(dim=-1)
                
                # Get best match
                score, idx = probs[0].max(dim=0)
                
                if score.item() > 0.3: # Threshold
                    label = classes[idx.item()]
                    predictions.append({
                        "label": label,
                        "start": i / 48000.0,
                        "end": min((i + chunk_samples) / 48000.0, len(audio_array)/48000.0),
                        "confidence": score.item()
                    })
                    
            return predictions

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error in AudioAdapter predict: {e}")
            return []

    def transcribe(self, audio_path):
        """
        Uses Faster-Whisper to transcribe speech.
        """
        model = self.load_whisper()
        if not model: return []
        
        segments, info = model.transcribe(audio_path, beam_size=5)
        
        results = []
        for segment in segments:
            results.append({
                "label": "speech",
                "text": segment.text,
                "start": segment.start,
                "end": segment.end,
                "confidence": segment.avg_logprob # Not exactly confidence 0-1 but usable
            })
        return results

    def retrain(self, project):
        """
        For Audio, 'retraining' currently involves exporting the verified dataset
        to a standard format (JSON/CSV) so external models can be trained.
        """
        print("Exporting Audio Dataset (Reinforcement Step)...")
        annotations = project.session.get("annotations", {})
        
        export_data = []
        for filename, data in annotations.items():
            objects = data.get("objects", [])
            if not objects: continue
            
            entry = {
                "audio_file": filename,
                "events": objects
            }
            export_data.append(entry)
            
        # Save to dataset dir
        export_path = os.path.join(project.dataset_dir, "audio_dataset_export.json")
        os.makedirs(project.dataset_dir, exist_ok=True)
        
        with open(export_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(export_data, f, indent=4)
            
        print(f"Exported {len(export_data)} annotated files to {export_path}")
        return export_path

import os
import json
import joblib
import torch
import numpy as np
import librosa
from sklearn.neural_network import MLPClassifier
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from src.adapters.base_adapter import BaseAdapter

# Try to import Transformers CLAP
try:
    from transformers import ClapModel, ClapProcessor
    TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE = False

try:
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    WHISPER_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    WHISPER_AVAILABLE = False

class AudioAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    def __init__(self, project):
        super().__init__(project)
        self.project = project
        self.model = None
        self.processor = None
        self.whisper_model = None
        self.device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
        self.model_id = "laion/clap-htsat-unfused" # Standard HF model
        
        # Path to the custom classifier head
        self.classifier_path = os.path.join(project.training_runs_dir, "audio_classifier.pkl")
        self.scaler_path = os.path.join(project.training_runs_dir, "audio_scaler.pkl")
        self.classifier = None
        self.scaler = None
        self.load_custom_classifier()

    @property
    def name(self):
        return "clap"

    def load(self):
        if not TRANSFORMERS_AVAILABLE:
            print("Error: 'transformers' library not found or missing CLAP support.")
            return

        print(f"Loading CLAP ({self.model_id}) on {self.device}...")
        try:
            self.model = ClapModel.from_pretrained(self.model_id).to(self.device)
            self.processor = ClapProcessor.from_pretrained(self.model_id)
            print("CLAP loaded successfully.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error loading CLAP: {e}")

    def load_whisper(self):
        if not WHISPER_AVAILABLE:
            print("Error: 'faster-whisper' library not found.")
            return None
        
        if self.whisper_model is None:
            print(f"Loading Faster-Whisper (tiny) on {self.device}...")
            # Compute type: float16 on GPU, int8 on CPU usually
            compute_type = "float16" if self.device == "cuda" else "int8"
            try:
                self.whisper_model = WhisperModel("tiny", device=self.device, compute_type=compute_type)
                print("Faster-Whisper loaded.")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error loading Whisper: {e}")
        return self.whisper_model

    def load_custom_classifier(self):
        if os.path.exists(self.classifier_path) and os.path.exists(self.scaler_path):
            try:
                self.classifier = joblib.load(self.classifier_path)
                self.scaler = joblib.load(self.scaler_path)
                print("Loaded custom audio classifier.")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Failed to load custom classifier: {e}")

    def get_embedding(self, audio_fragment, sr=48000):
        """Generates CLAP audio embedding for a raw audio array."""
        if self.model is None: self.load()
        inputs = self.processor(audios=audio_fragment, sampling_rate=sr, return_tensors="pt").to(self.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = self.model.get_audio_features(**inputs)
        return outputs.cpu().numpy() # Returns (1, 512) usually

    def predict(self, audio_path, **kwargs):
        """
        Predicts sound events. If a custom classifier exists, uses it. 
        Otherwise falls back to zero-shot CLAP.
        """
        if self.model is None:
            self.load()
            if self.model is None: return []

        classes = kwargs.get("classes", [])
        
        try:
            # Load audio at 48k
            audio_array, sr = librosa.load(audio_path, sr=48000)
            chunk_duration = 5.0 
            chunk_samples = int(chunk_duration * 48000)
            
            predictions = []
            
            # Use custom classifier if available and classes match known classes (simplified: just use it)
            use_custom = self.classifier is not None
            
            # Prepare text inputs for Zero-Shot if needed
            text_probs_needed = not use_custom and classes
            if text_probs_needed:
                 text_inputs = self.processor(text=classes, return_tensors="pt", padding=True).to(self.device)

            for i in range(0, len(audio_array), chunk_samples):
                chunk = audio_array[i:i+chunk_samples]
                if len(chunk) < 2000: break 
                
                # --- Custom Classifier Path ---
                if use_custom:
                    emb = self.get_embedding(chunk, sr=48000)
                    emb_scaled = self.scaler.transform(emb)
                    probs = self.classifier.predict_proba(emb_scaled)[0]
                    max_idx = np.argmax(probs)
                    conf = probs[max_idx]
                    
                    if conf > 0.5: # Confidence threshold
                        label = self.classifier.classes_[max_idx]
                        if label != "_background_": # Ignore background class
                            predictions.append({
                                "label": label,
                                "start": i / 48000.0,
                                "end": min((i + chunk_samples) / 48000.0, len(audio_array)/48000.0),
                                "confidence": float(conf)
                            })

                # --- Zero-Shot Path ---
                elif text_probs_needed:
                    audio_inputs = self.processor(audios=chunk, sampling_rate=48000, return_tensors="pt").to(self.device)
                    with torch.no_grad():
                        outputs = self.model(**text_inputs, **audio_inputs)
                    probs = outputs.logits_per_audio.softmax(dim=-1)
                    score, idx = probs[0].max(dim=0)
                    
                    if score.item() > 0.3: 
                        label = classes[idx.item()]
                        predictions.append({
                            "label": label,
                            "start": i / 48000.0,
                            "end": min((i + chunk_samples) / 48000.0, len(audio_array)/48000.0),
                            "confidence": score.item()
                        })
                    
            return predictions

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error in AudioAdapter predict: {e}")
            return []

    def transcribe(self, audio_path):
        """ Uses Faster-Whisper to transcribe speech. """
        model = self.load_whisper()
        if not model: return []
        segments, info = model.transcribe(audio_path, beam_size=5)
        results = []
        for segment in segments:
            results.append({
                "label": "speech",
                "text": segment.text,
                "start": segment.start,
                "end": segment.end,
                "confidence": segment.avg_logprob 
            })
        return results

    def retrain(self, project):
        """
        Trains a custom Classifier (MLP) on top of CLAP embeddings.
        1. Extracts embeddings for all annotated segments (Positives).
        2. Extracts random embeddings from unannotated areas (Negatives / Background).
        3. Trains MLPClassifier.
        4. Saves the classifier to be used in predict().
        """
        print("Starting Audio Reinforcement Training...")
        annotations = project.session.get("annotations", {})
        
        X = []
        y = []
        
        # 1. Collect Positives
        annotated_files = 0
        for filename, data in annotations.items():
            objects = data.get("objects", [])
            if not objects: continue
            
            file_path = os.path.join(project.audio_dir_source, filename)
            if not os.path.exists(file_path): continue
            
            try:
                audio_full, sr = librosa.load(file_path, sr=48000)
                file_len = len(audio_full) / 48000.0
                annotated_files += 1
                
                # Mask to track annotated regions for background sampling
                mask = np.zeros(len(audio_full), dtype=bool)

                for obj in objects:
                    # Skip if it's a transcription or missing times
                    if obj.get("type") == "transcription": continue
                    if "start" not in obj or "end" not in obj: continue
                    
                    label = obj["label"]
                    start_sample = int(obj["start"] * 48000)
                    end_sample = int(obj["end"] * 48000)
                    
                    # Clip
                    start_sample = max(0, start_sample)
                    end_sample = min(len(audio_full), end_sample)
                    
                    if end_sample - start_sample < 2000: continue # Skip too short
                    
                    # Extract and embed
                    fragment = audio_full[start_sample:end_sample]
                    emb = self.get_embedding(fragment)
                    X.append(emb[0])
                    y.append(label)
                    
                    # Mark region
                    mask[start_sample:end_sample] = True

                # 2. Collect Negatives (Background) from this file
                # Extract a few random chunks from unmasked areas
                unmasked_indices = np.where(~mask)[0]
                if len(unmasked_indices) > 48000 * 2: # At least 2 seconds of silence
                    # Try to find continuous chunks
                    # Simplification: Just pick random start points that are unmasked and hope for 1s
                    num_bg_samples = max(1, len(objects)) # Balance 1:1 roughly
                    for _ in range(num_bg_samples):
                        start_idx = np.random.choice(unmasked_indices)
                        end_idx = start_idx + 48000 * 2 # 2 second background chunk
                        if end_idx < len(audio_full) and not np.any(mask[start_idx:end_idx]):
                            bg_fragment = audio_full[start_idx:end_idx]
                            emb = self.get_embedding(bg_fragment)
                            X.append(emb[0])
                            y.append("_background_")
                            
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error processing {filename}: {e}")

        if len(X) < 5:
            print("Not enough data to train (need at least 5 samples).")
            return None
        
        print(f"Training on {len(X)} samples from {annotated_files} files.")
        X = np.array(X)
        y = np.array(y)
        
        # Train
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
        
        clf = MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(128, 64), max_iter=500, random_state=42)
        clf.fit(X_scaled, y)
        
        # Save
        os.makedirs(project.training_runs_dir, exist_ok=True)
        joblib.dump(clf, self.classifier_path)
        joblib.dump(scaler, self.scaler_path)
        
        self.classifier = clf
        self.scaler = scaler
        
        print(f"Classifier saved to {self.classifier_path}")
        return self.classifier_path

Replaces text within a file. By default, replaces a single occurrence, but can replace multiple occurrences when `expected_replacements` is specified. This tool requires providing significant context around the change to ensure precise targeting. Always use the read_file tool to examine the file's current content before attempting a text replacement.
      
      The user has the ability to modify the `new_string` content. If modified, this will be stated in the response.
      
      Expectation for required parameters:
      1. `old_string` MUST be the exact literal text to replace (including all whitespace, indentation, newlines, and surrounding code etc.).
      2. `new_string` MUST be the exact literal text to replace `old_string` with (also including all whitespace, indentation, newlines, and surrounding code etc.). Ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic and that `old_string` and `new_string` are different.
      3. `instruction` is the detailed instruction of what needs to be changed. It is important to Make it specific and detailed so developers or large language models can understand what needs to be changed and perform the changes on their own if necessary. 
      4. NEVER escape `old_string` or `new_string`, that would break the exact literal text requirement.
      **Important:** If ANY of the above are not satisfied, the tool will fail. CRITICAL for `old_string`: Must uniquely identify the single instance to change. Include at least 3 lines of context BEFORE and AFTER the target text, matching whitespace and indentation precisely. If this string matches multiple locations, or does not match exactly, the tool will fail.

import os
import cv2
import numpy as np
import random
from PIL import Image

class SyntheticGenerator:
    def __init__(self, project):
        self.project = project
        self.output_dir = self.project.image_dir_source
        # os.makedirs(self.output_dir, exist_ok=True) # It exists by definition

    def generate_variants(self, image_path, annotations, count=5):
        """
        Generates synthetic variants of a single image and its annotations.
        Supports Bounding Boxes.
        """
        if not os.path.exists(image_path):
            return []

        img = cv2.imread(image_path)
        if img is None:
            return []
        
        h, w = img.shape[:2]
        base_name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(image_path))[0]
        
        generated_files = []
        generated_annotations = {}

        for i in range(count):
            # Randomly select an augmentation strategy
            aug_type = random.choice(["flip", "noise", "brightness", "blur"])
            
            new_img = img.copy()
            new_anns = [ann.copy() for ann in annotations] # Deep copy dicts
            suffix = f"syn_{aug_type}_{i}"
            
            if aug_type == "flip":
                # Horizontal Flip
                new_img = cv2.flip(new_img, 1)
                for ann in new_anns:
                    if ann["type"] == "bbox":
                        x1, y1, x2, y2 = ann["points"]
                        # Flip coordinates
                        nx1 = w - x2
                        nx2 = w - x1
                        ann["points"] = [nx1, y1, nx2, y2]
                    # Polygon flip logic would go here
                    
            elif aug_type == "noise":
                row, col, ch = new_img.shape
                mean = 0
                var = 0.05
                sigma = var**0.5
                gauss = np.random.normal(mean, sigma, (row, col, ch))
                gauss = gauss.reshape(row, col, ch)
                noisy = new_img / 255.0 + gauss
                new_img = (np.clip(noisy, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)

            elif aug_type == "brightness":
                value = random.randint(-50, 50)
                hsv = cv2.cvtColor(new_img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)
                h, s, v = cv2.split(hsv)
                lim = 255 - value
                v[v > lim] = 255
                v[v <= lim] = np.add(v[v <= lim], value)
                final_hsv = cv2.merge((h, s, v))
                new_img = cv2.cvtColor(final_hsv, cv2.COLOR_HSV2BGR)
                
            elif aug_type == "blur":
                ksize = random.choice([3, 5, 7])
                new_img = cv2.GaussianBlur(new_img, (ksize, ksize), 0)

            # Save Result
            new_filename = f"{base_name}_{suffix}.jpg"
            save_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, new_filename)
            cv2.imwrite(save_path, new_img)
            
            generated_files.append(new_filename)
            generated_annotations[new_filename] = {"objects": new_anns, "image_tags": ["synthetic"]}

        return generated_files, generated_annotations

import os
import subprocess
from ultralytics import YOLO
from src.adapters.base_adapter import BaseAdapter
from src.training.dataset_manager import build_dataset

class YOLOAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    def __init__(self, project, model_path=None):
        super().__init__(project)
        self.project = project
        self.model_path = model_path or project.active_model
        self.model = None

    @property
    def name(self):
        return "yolov8" # Identifier for logic switching if needed

    def load(self):
        """Load model weights into memory."""
        print(f"Loading YOLO model from: {self.model_path}")
        self.model = YOLO(self.model_path)

    def predict(self, image_path, **kwargs):
        if self.model is None:
            self.load()

        # Run inference
        results = self.model.predict(
            source=image_path,
            save=False,
            save_crop=False,
            project=self.project.root_path,
            name="predictions_log",
            exist_ok=True,
            verbose=False,
            conf=kwargs.get("conf_threshold", 0.25)
        )
        
        out = []
        for r in results:
            boxes = getattr(r, "boxes", None)
            if boxes is None:
                continue
            for b in boxes:
                xyxy = b.xyxy[0].tolist()
                conf = float(b.conf[0])
                cls = int(b.cls[0])
                label = self.model.names.get(cls, str(cls))
                x1, y1, x2, y2 = map(int, xyxy)
                out.append(
                    {
                        "label": label,
                        "x1": x1,
                        "y1": y1,
                        "x2": x2,
                        "y2": y2,
                        "confidence": conf,
                    }
                )
        return out

    def retrain(self, project):
        """
        Triggers fine-tuning using the project data.
        1. Builds the YOLO dataset from current session.json annotations.
        2. Runs 'yolo train'.
        3. Returns the path to the new best model.
        """
        print("Building dataset for retraining...")
        # Access annotations from the project session
        annotations = project.session.get("annotations", {})
        
        # We need the label list. It's stored in project/dataset/labels.json usually,
        # but the GUI manages it. We can try to read it or infer it.
        # Best practice: The Project object should manage the label list state, 
        # but currently it's in a file managed by the GUI.
        # Let's try to read the label file.
        label_file = os.path.join(project.dataset_dir, "labels.json")
        import json
        label_list = []
        if os.path.exists(label_file):
            with open(label_file, 'r') as f:
                data = json.load(f)
                label_list = data.get("labels", [])
        
        if not label_list:
            print("Warning: No labels found in labels.json. Dataset build might fail.")
            
        build_dataset(project, annotations, label_list)

        print("Starting YOLO training command...")
        # Define a unique run name based on timestamp or increment
        run_name = "reinforce_run"
        
        # CLI Command
        cmd = [
            "yolo",
            "task=detect",
            "mode=train",
            f"data={os.path.join(project.dataset_dir, 'data.yaml')}",
            f"model={self.model_path}",
            f"project={project.training_runs_dir}",
            f"name={run_name}",
            "epochs=10",
            "imgsz=640",
            "exist_ok=True" # Overwrite run to save space/time for this prototype
        ]
        
        # Use subprocess
        # On Windows, we might need shell=True for 'yolo' if it's a bat file, 
        # but usually 'yolo' is an exe in Scripts.
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
        
        # Locate new weights
        best_model_path = os.path.join(
            project.training_runs_dir, run_name, "weights", "best.pt"
        )
        
        if os.path.exists(best_model_path):
            print(f"Training success. New weights: {best_model_path}")
            self.model_path = best_model_path
            self.load() # Reload the new model
            return best_model_path
        else:
            print("Error: training finished but 'best.pt' not found.")
            return None

    def get_last_trained_model_path(self):
        return self.model_path

import os
import random
import numpy as np
import librosa
import soundfile as sf

class AudioAugmentor:
    def __init__(self, project):
        self.project = project
        self.output_dir = self.project.audio_dir_source
    
    def generate_variants(self, audio_path, annotations, count=3):
        """
        Generates synthetic variants of an audio file and its annotations.
        Supports: Gaussian Noise, Pitch Shift, Time Stretch.
        """
        if not os.path.exists(audio_path):
            return [], {}
            
        try:
            y, sr = librosa.load(audio_path, sr=None)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error loading {audio_path}: {e}")
            return [], {}
            
        base_name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(audio_path))[0]
        ext = os.path.splitext(audio_path)[1]
        
        generated_files = []
        generated_annotations = {}
        
        for i in range(count):
            aug_type = random.choice(["noise", "pitch", "shift"])
            suffix = f"syn_{aug_type}_{i}"
            new_y = y.copy()
            new_anns = [ann.copy() for ann in annotations] # Deep copy
            
            if aug_type == "noise":
                # Add Gaussian Noise
                noise_amp = 0.005 * np.random.uniform() * np.amax(new_y)
                new_y = new_y + noise_amp * np.random.normal(size=len(new_y))
                
            elif aug_type == "pitch":
                # Pitch Shift (changes pitch without changing speed)
                n_steps = random.uniform(-2, 2)
                new_y = librosa.effects.pitch_shift(new_y, sr=sr, n_steps=n_steps)
                
            elif aug_type == "shift":
                # Time Shift (Roll)
                shift_amt = int(random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2) * len(new_y))
                new_y = np.roll(new_y, shift_amt)
                
                # Shift annotations accordingly
                shift_sec = shift_amt / sr
                valid_anns = []
                for ann in new_anns:
                    if "start" in ann and "end" in ann:
                        start = ann["start"] + shift_sec
                        end = ann["end"] + shift_sec
                        duration = len(new_y) / sr
                        
                        # Handle wrapping or clipping
                        # For simple roll, the event wraps around. 
                        # We will just clip/discard for simplicity to keep it valid
                        if 0 <= start < duration and 0 <= end <= duration:
                            ann["start"] = start
                            ann["end"] = end
                            valid_anns.append(ann)
                new_anns = valid_anns

            # Save
            new_filename = f"{base_name}_{suffix}{ext}"
            save_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, new_filename)
            
            # soundfile expects data, samplerate
            sf.write(save_path, new_y, sr)
            
            generated_files.append(new_filename)
            generated_annotations[new_filename] = {"objects": new_anns}
            
        return generated_files, generated_annotations

Content from @NeuroLoop.md:
NeuroLoop: Multimodal HITL Platform (Developer Documentation)

NeuroLoop (formerly EchoLearn) is a local, privacy-first desktop application designed to accelerate the creation of custom AI/ML models for Vision (Object Detection/Segmentation applied to Images & Video) and Audio (Sound Event Detection/Classification), by replacing the traditional Label → Train pipeline with a continuous Reinforcement Learning Loop powered by interactive Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) feedback, synthetic data enrichment, and incremental retraining.

It transforms model training into this cycle:

Bootstrap: Auto-label using foundation models (e.g., Florence-2, SAM 2, CLAP).

Interact: Human corrects only hard or uncertain cases via dedicated GUIs.

Reinforce: Corrections accumulate and trigger background model retraining.

Loop: Models improve with minimal user effort over time.

This documentation also includes guidelines on UML diagrams (class, sequence, use case, component), design artifacts, and a suggested implementation plan with estimated timelines and milestones to support development clarity, traceability, and collaboration.

1. Project Vision & Core Philosophy

Mission:
Enable developers, researchers, and practitioners to build high-quality multimodal AI systems without requiring deep expertise in annotation tooling or training pipelines.

Design Principles:

Local First & Privacy-Centered — All data stays local unless explicitly configured otherwise.

Extensible Modular Design — Swap models and data processing modules easily using the Adapter Pattern.

Human-Machine Symbiosis — The system actively learns from human corrections for faster model convergence.

Multimodal Capability — Handle both vision and audio workflows with tailored user experiences.

Continuous Learning Cycle — Rather than static training, models improve incrementally as users interact.

2. Technical Architecture
Directory Structure
NeuroLoop/
├── projects/
│   └── [project_name]/
│       ├── project.json      # Static config (paths, modalities, enabled models)
│       ├── session.json      # Progress state (cursor, annotations, buffer counters)
│       └── dataset/          # Generated datasets (vision/audio unified outputs)
├── src/
│   ├── main.py               # Launch point: project selection → GUI
│   ├── managers/
│   │   ├── project_manager.py
│   │   └── model_manager.py
│   ├── adapters/
│   │   ├── base_adapter.py
│   │   ├── yolo_adapter.py
│   │   ├── florence_adapter.py
│   │   ├── sam2_adapter.py
│   │   └── audio_adapter.py
│   ├── gui/
│   │   ├── vision_gui.py
│   │   └── audio_gui.py
│   └── training/
│       ├── dataset_manager.py
│       └── synthetic_generator.py
└── pretrained_models/        # Local cache of model weights

3. Core Workflows & Logic
Project Lifecycle

Initiate Project:

Create project, choose modality (vision, audio, or mixed).

Configure base models and auto-labeling options.

Auto-Label & Annotate:

Vision (bounding boxes, polygons/segmentation).

Audio (wave/time span labels).

Both GUIs present tailored annotation tools and model suggestions.

Correction Tracking:

Each correction increments a counter in session.json.

Reinforcement Retraining Loop:

After a configurable threshold of corrections, system triggers background retraining.

The retrained model replaces previous weights, improving subsequent auto-labels.

Synthetic Data:

Apply configurable synthetic transformations to augment the dataset.

Synthetic data is integrated into retraining datasets.

4. Guided Annotation Standards

Structured annotation schemas are enforced to ensure dataset quality.

Vision Annotations

Bounding Boxes: x, y, width, height plus label + confidence.

Polygons/Masks: Arbitrary coordinate lists for segmentation.

Video Tracking: Object IDs that persist across frames.

Audio Annotations

Segment Tags: [start_time, end_time, label] — Supports multi-label events.

Confidence Tracking: Auto-label confidence + human adjustment.

Clear annotation standards enable proper dataset export and downstream training.

5. Dataset Generation & Export

Output formats supported include:

Vision: YOLO (primary), COCO/CSV (optional converters).

Audio: JSON/CSV sequences of labeled segments.

Datasets support mixed annotation types and can be exported for external training environments as needed.

6. Synthetic Data & Augmentation

Synthetic generation leverages:

Classic augmentations — flips, brightness, noise, blur.

Compositional scene augmentations — placing objects in variable contexts.

Synthetic samples are flagged and added to project datasets for human review before training.

7. Model Reinforcement Learning Loop

Instead of single-shot training:

The system incrementally retrains with corrected and synthetic data.

Corrections drive model improvements where it matters most.

Background jobs minimize UI interruption.

8. Technology & Libraries
Layer	Stack / Libraries
GUI	tkinter
Vision Training	ultralytics (YOLO)
Auto-Labeling	Florence-2 (Vision), CLAP (Audio)
Segmentation	SAM 2
Audio Visualization	librosa + matplotlib
9. Design Artifacts: UML & Architecture Diagrams

Including UML and other visual models improves documentation quality, onboarding, and team alignment. Visual artifacts make architecture and interaction clearer, reduce miscommunication, and help plan incremental work.

A. Use Case Diagrams

Map actors (e.g., Annotator, Trainer) to core tasks (Annotate, Retrain, Generate Synthetic Data).

B. Class Diagrams

Show structure of core modules such as:

ProjectManager

ModelManager

BaseAdapter & specific adapters

DatasetManager

SyntheticGenerator

GUIs (Vision, Audio)

Best practices include focused, well-named models and separating high-level overview diagrams from detailed implementation diagrams.

C. Sequence Diagrams

Visualize interactions like:
User → Vision GUI → Model Adapter → Prediction
UserCorrection → Session → Retrain Trigger → Model Update

D. Component Diagrams

Break down larger subsystems (Vision, Audio, Training) to show relationships and dependencies.

Use standard UML notations, focus diagrams on conveying intent, and keep diagrams synchronized with actual implementation states.

Optional Tooling:

Tools like Lucidchart, Visual Paradigm, or PlantUML make it easy to author and maintain diagrams collaboratively.

10. Implementation Plan, Timeline & Milestones

To structure development and manage risk, organize work into incremental phases with clear milestones. A strong project plan should describe work products such as UML diagrams, architectural specs, code modules, and test plans alongside estimates of effort and scheduling.

Phase 1 — Foundations (Weeks 1–4)

Establish architecture, data structures, adapter interfaces.

Build skeleton GUIs for vision and audio.

Produce initial UML diagrams (class + use-case + components).

Milestone: Architecture specs + initial diagram set complete.

Phase 2 — Annotation + Auto-Labeling (Weeks 5–8)

Integrate Florence-2 (vision) and CLAP (audio) auto-labeling.

Finalize annotation workflows + schemas.

Refine sequence diagrams.

Milestone: Functional annotation + auto-labeling flows.

Phase 3 — Training Loop + Reinforcement (Weeks 9–12)

Build correction tracking and retraining scheduler.

Connect YOLO incremental training.

Track and visualize correction impact.

Milestone: Closed reinforcement loop operational.

Phase 4 — Synthetic & Export Workflows (Weeks 13–16)

Implement synthetic data generation pipelines.

Export utilities for dataset formats.

Add versioning and analytics dashboards.

Milestone: End-to-end workflow from raw media → trained model → export.

11. Usage & Getting Started

Launch Application

# Activate virtual environment
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Run NeuroLoop
python -m src.main


Add a New Model

Create a new adapter subclass under src/adapters/.

def _setup_menu(self):
        menubar = tk.Menu(self.master)
        
        # Tools Menu
        tools_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        tools_menu.add_command(label="Generate Synthetic Data (Current Image)", command=self.generate_synthetic_data)
        menubar.add_cascade(label="Tools", menu=tools_menu)
        
        # View Menu
        view_menu = tk.Menu(menubar, tearoff=0)
        view_menu.add_command(label="Project Dashboard", command=self.show_dashboard)
        menubar.add_cascade(label="View", menu=view_menu)
        
        self.master.config(menu=menubar)

    def show_dashboard(self):
        explorer = DatasetExplorer(self.project)
        stats = explorer.get_stats()
        
        dash = tk.Toplevel(self.master)
        dash.title("Project Dashboard")
        dash.geometry("400x300")
        
        tk.Label(dash, text="Project Statistics", font=("Arial", 14, "bold")).pack(pady=10)
        
        frame = tk.Frame(dash, padx=20)
        frame.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
        
        tk.Label(frame, text=f"Total Files: {stats['total_files']}").pack(anchor="w")
        tk.Label(frame, text=f"Annotated Files: {stats['annotated_files']}").pack(anchor="w")
        
        tk.Label(frame, text="Class Distribution:", font=("Arial", 10, "bold")).pack(anchor="w", pady=(10, 5))
        
        list_frame = tk.Frame(frame)
        list_frame.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
        
        lb = tk.Listbox(list_frame)
        lb.pack(side=tk.LEFT, fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
        
        scrollbar = tk.Scrollbar(list_frame)
        scrollbar.pack(side=tk.RIGHT, fill=tk.Y)
        lb.config(yscrollcommand=scrollbar.set)
        scrollbar.config(command=lb.yview)
        
        for label, count in stats["class_distribution"].items():
            lb.insert(tk.END, f"{label}: {count}")

    def _setup_ui(self):

    @property
    def name(self):
        return "sam2"

    def load(self):
        if not SAM2_AVAILABLE:
            print("Error: sam2 library not found. Please install it to use SAM2Adapter.")
            return

        print(f"Loading SAM 2 on {self.device}...")
        # Check if checkpoint exists in pretrained_models
        possible_paths = [

                break
             
        if not ckpt_path:

            return

        try:
            # Image Predictor
            model = build_sam2(self.model_cfg, ckpt_path, device=self.device)
            self.predictor = SAM2ImagePredictor(model)
            
            # Video Predictor
            self.video_predictor = build_sam2_video_predictor(self.model_cfg, ckpt_path, device=self.device)
            
            print("SAM 2 loaded successfully.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error loading SAM 2: {e}")

    def mask_to_polygon(self, mask):
        """
        Converts a binary mask (H, W) to a list of (x, y) points.
        """
        mask = mask.astype(np.uint8) * 255
        contours, _ = cv2.findContours(mask, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
        
        if not contours:
            return []
            
        # Take the largest contour
        c = max(contours, key=cv2.contourArea)
        # Approximate to reduce points
        epsilon = 0.005 * cv2.arcLength(c, True)
        approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(c, epsilon, True)
        
        return [point[0].tolist() for point in approx]

    def predict(self, image_path, **kwargs):
        """
        Predicts masks given prompts.
        Kwargs:
            boxes: List of [x1, y1, x2, y2]
        """
        if self.predictor is None:
            self.load()
            if self.predictor is None: return []

        image = Image.open(image_path)
        if image.mode != "RGB":
            image = image.convert("RGB")
        image_np = np.array(image)

        self.predictor.set_image(image_np)

        input_boxes = kwargs.get("boxes", None)
        predictions = []

        if input_boxes:
            input_boxes = np.array(input_boxes)
            # SAM 2 batch prediction
            masks, scores, logits = self.predictor.predict(
                box=input_boxes,
                multimask_output=False
            )
            
            # Masks shape: (N, 1, H, W) -> squeeze to (N, H, W)
            if masks.ndim == 4:
                masks = masks.squeeze(1)

            for i, mask in enumerate(masks):
                poly_points = self.mask_to_polygon(mask)
                if not poly_points: continue
                
                predictions.append({
                    "label": "mask", 
                    "type": "polygon",
                    "points": poly_points,
                    "confidence": float(scores[i][0]) if scores.ndim > 1 else float(scores[i])
                })
        
        return predictions

    def track_object(self, video_path, start_frame_idx, box, label="object"):
        """
        Uses SAM 2 Video Predictor to track an object from a starting box.
        
        Args:
            video_path (str): Path to the video file.
            start_frame_idx (int): Frame index to start tracking from.
            box (list): [x1, y1, x2, y2] bounding box.
            label (str): Label to apply to tracked objects.
            
        Returns:
            dict: { frame_idx (int): annotation_dict }
        """
        if self.video_predictor is None:
            self.load()
            if self.video_predictor is None: return {}

        # 1. Extract frames to temp dir
        # SAM 2 requires a directory of JPEG/PNG frames.
        # We'll use a temp directory.
        temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="sam2_frames_")
        print(f"Extracting frames to {temp_dir}...")
        
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)
        frame_count = 0
        while True:
            ret, frame = cap.read()
            if not ret: break
            # Save as 00000.jpg, 00001.jpg etc.
            frame_name = f"{frame_count:05d}.jpg"
            cv2.imwrite(os.path.join(temp_dir, frame_name), frame)
            frame_count += 1
        cap.release()
        
        if frame_count == 0:
            shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)
            return {}

        try:
            # 2. Initialize State
            print("Initializing inference state...")
            inference_state = self.video_predictor.init_state(video_path=temp_dir)

            # 3. Add Prompt (Box)
            # Note: SAM 2 expects obj_id (int), frame_idx (int), box (np.array [x1, y1, x2, y2])
            ann_obj_id = 1  # We only track one object at a time for this simple API
            prompts = {} 
            
            _, out_obj_ids, out_mask_logits = self.video_predictor.add_new_points_or_box(
                inference_state=inference_state,
                frame_idx=start_frame_idx,
                obj_id=ann_obj_id,
                box=np.array(box, dtype=np.float32)
            )

            # 4. Propagate
            print("Propagating tracking...")
            # Propagate forward from start frame
            results = {}
            
            for out_frame_idx, out_obj_ids, out_mask_logits in self.video_predictor.propagate_in_video(inference_state):
                if out_frame_idx < start_frame_idx: continue # Skip past frames if any
                
                # Convert masks to polygons/boxes
                # out_mask_logits shape: (N_obj, H, W)
                for i, obj_id in enumerate(out_obj_ids):
                    mask = (out_mask_logits[i] > 0.0).cpu().numpy().squeeze()
                    
                    # Convert to polygon
                    points = self.mask_to_polygon(mask)
                    if not points: continue
                    
                    # Also calculate bounding box from polygon for compatibility
                    # Simple min/max
                    pts = np.array(points)
                    x1, y1 = pts.min(axis=0)
                    x2, y2 = pts.max(axis=0)
                    
                    results[out_frame_idx] = {
                        "type": "polygon",
                        "label": label,
                        "points": points,
                        "bbox": [float(x1), float(y1), float(x2), float(y2)],
                        "confidence": 1.0 # Propagated
                    }
            
            return results

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error during SAM 2 tracking: {e}")
            return {}
        finally:
            # Cleanup
            shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)

    def retrain(self, annotations):
        pass

        model_frame = tk.LabelFrame(self.control_panel, text="Model Control", padx=5, pady=5)
        model_frame.pack(fill=tk.X, pady=5)
        tk.Button(model_frame, text="Track Object (SAM 2)", command=self.track_object).pack(fill=tk.X)

    def track_object(self):
        # 1. Get current video and frame
        vid_key = self.video_files[self.current_video_index]
        video_path = os.path.join(self.data_dir, vid_key)
        
        # 2. Get the LAST created bbox in this frame as the prompt
        frame_key = str(self.current_frame_idx)
        anns = self.user_annotations.get(vid_key, {}).get(frame_key, {}).get("objects", [])
        
        if not anns:
            messagebox.showinfo("SAM 2", "Draw a bounding box around the object to track first.")
            return
            
        # Assume last one is the prompt
        prompt_ann = anns[-1]
        if prompt_ann["type"] != "bbox":
             messagebox.showinfo("SAM 2", "Please use a bounding box as prompt.")
             return
             
        box = prompt_ann["points"] # [x1, y1, x2, y2] scaled? 
        # Points are stored scaled if self.scale was used? 
        # Let's check: "points": [int(min(x1, x2) / self.scale), ...]
        # Yes, they are in original image coords. Perfect.
        
        label = prompt_ann["label"]
        
        self.stats_label.config(text="SAM 2: Extracting frames & Tracking... (This may take a while)")
        self.master.update()
        
        # 3. Call Adapter
        results = self.adapters["sam2"].track_object(video_path, self.current_frame_idx, box, label)
        
        if not results:
            messagebox.showerror("SAM 2", "Tracking failed or returned no results.")
            self.update_stats()
            return
            
        # 4. Merge results
        count = 0
        self.user_annotations.setdefault(vid_key, {})
        for frame_idx, ann in results.items():
            f_key = str(frame_idx)
            self.user_annotations[vid_key].setdefault(f_key, {"objects": []})
            self.user_annotations[vid_key][f_key]["objects"].append(ann)
            count += 1
            
        self.update_stats()
        messagebox.showinfo("SAM 2", f"Tracked object across {count} frames.")
        self.redraw_annotations()

    def _setup_annotation_panel(self):

import numpy as np
import random

class ActiveLearner:
    def __init__(self, project, model_adapter):
        self.project = project
        self.model_adapter = model_adapter
        
    def uncertainty_sampling(self, unlabelled_files, n_samples=5, strategy="least_confidence"):
        """
        Selects the top N most uncertain samples from the unlabelled set.
        Strategies: 'least_confidence', 'entropy', 'random'.
        """
        if not unlabelled_files:
            return []
            
        if strategy == "random":
            return random.sample(unlabelled_files, min(len(unlabelled_files), n_samples))

        scores = []
        print(f"Active Learning: Scoring {len(unlabelled_files)} files using {strategy}...")
        
        for f in unlabelled_files:
            # We need predictions to calculate uncertainty.
            # This can be slow if we run it on all files. 
            # In production, we'd cache these or run in background.
            # For prototype, we'll limit to checking a subset if too large, or just run it.
            
            # TODO: Add caching of predictions so we don't re-predict unchanged files
            
            file_path = ""
            # Determine path based on modality
            if hasattr(self.project, "image_dir_source"):
                 file_path = os.path.join(self.project.image_dir_source, f)
            elif hasattr(self.project, "audio_dir_source"):
                 file_path = os.path.join(self.project.audio_dir_source, f)
                 
            if not os.path.exists(file_path): continue
            
            # Predict
            try:
                preds = self.model_adapter.predict(file_path)
            except:
                preds = []
            
            score = 0.0
            if not preds:
                # No predictions = High uncertainty? Or Low?
                # Usually implies model missed everything. 
                # Let's treat empty as high uncertainty (score 0.0 confidence).
                confidences = [0.0]
            else:
                confidences = [p.get("confidence", 0.0) for p in preds]
            
            if strategy == "least_confidence":
                # Score = 1 - Max(Confidence)
                # We want to maximize this score (higher = more uncertain)
                max_conf = max(confidences) if confidences else 0.0
                score = 1.0 - max_conf
                
            elif strategy == "entropy":
                # Entropy = -Sum(p * log(p))
                # This requires full probability distribution over classes, 
                # but YOLO/detection usually gives discrete box confidences.
                # Approx: Average 1-confidence? Or just stick to LC for detections.
                pass
            
            scores.append((f, score))
            
        # Sort by score descending (Highest uncertainty first)
        scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        
        # Return top N filenames
        return [x[0] for x in scores[:n_samples]]

def suggest_next_image(self):
        # Identify unlabelled files
        all_files = set(self.data_ids)
        labelled_files = set(self.user_annotations.keys())
        unlabelled = list(all_files - labelled_files)
        
        if not unlabelled:
            messagebox.showinfo("Active Learning", "All images are already annotated!")
            return
            
        self.update_stats("Active Learning: Analyzing unlabelled images...")
        self.master.update()
        
        # Sample a subset to keep UI responsive (e.g. 10 random files from unlabelled)
        # In a real app, this would run in background
        subset = random.sample(unlabelled, min(len(unlabelled), 10))
        
        suggestions = self.active_learner.uncertainty_sampling(subset, n_samples=1, strategy="least_confidence")
        
        if suggestions:
            target = suggestions[0]
            if target in self.data_ids:
                idx = self.data_ids.index(target)
                self.index = idx
                self.show_current_data()
                self.update_stats(f"Jumped to suggested image: {target}")
            else:
                self.update_stats("Error finding suggested image.")
        else:
            self.update_stats("Could not determine a suggestion.")

    def run(self):

    *   Integrated it into `VisionGUI` with a "Suggest Next (Active Learning)" button that automatically navigates to the most "confusing" unlabelled image.

    *   Created `src/utils/theme.py` to manage application styling.
    *   Applied the Dark Theme to `VisionGUI`, `AudioGUI`, and `VideoGUI`, giving the application a unified, professional look.
    *   Marked as complete in `TODO.md`.

This is a significant UI pivot. To achieve a **Label Studio-like experience** (Modern, Dark Mode by default, Modular, Card-based Project View) while keeping it a local Python desktop app, we will migrate from standard `tkinter` to **`customtkinter`**.

It provides modern, rounded, high-DPI aware widgets and a native Dark Mode, similar to modern web interfaces, without requiring a rewrite in JavaScript/React.

Here is the plan to modernize the `src/gui` architecture:

1.  **New Structure**: Modularize `src/gui` into `components/`, `windows/`, and `utils/`.
2.  **Dashboard**: Replace the simple list dialog with a Card-based Project Dashboard.
3.  **Workspace**: Create a unified "Studio" window with a collapsible sidebar and tool palette.
4.  **Settings**: Implement a persistent global `options` system.

### Step 1: Add Dependencies

I will add `customtkinter` to the requirements.

thoughts.subject: Contemplating the Rebuild
thoughts.description:
\n\n

I'm starting by clarifying the objective: to modernize NeuroLoop's GUI, drawing inspiration from Label Studio. This initial step is crucial. I'll need to define what "modern" means in this context – usability, aesthetics, or perhaps underlying architecture. Grasping the user's intent is paramount before delving into design or implementation.

thoughts.subject: Analyzing the Modernization
thoughts.description:
\n\n

I've begun to dissect the "modern" requirement. Considering Label Studio as a model, the jump from Tkinter to a web-based approach appears ideal. However, the desktop app constraint presents a challenge. I'm weighing the trade-offs: sticking with modernized Tkinter versus venturing into web technologies within a desktop wrapper. My priority is a solution that elegantly replicates the target's look and feel while remaining performant and user-friendly.

thoughts.subject: Assessing the Tech Stack
thoughts.description:
\n\n

My evaluation of the technology options has intensified. While `customtkinter` offers a quick aesthetic fix, its limitations quickly become apparent. I've been experimenting with PyQt as the next logical step to get a "Label Studio" look, but the learning curve is steep, and the licensing complicates things. However, PyQt's powerful widgets and design capabilities seem essential for the complexity envisioned. I am also considering a full rewrite to a web-based approach using Electron but this is likely overkill at this stage.

thoughts.subject: Planning the Refactor
thoughts.description:
\n\n

My current thinking centers on solidifying a phased approach. First, swapping `tkinter` for `customtkinter` to achieve a modern appearance without major code disruption. Then, a careful restructuring of the `./gui` directory, clearly separating widgets and logic. Finally, I will address the settings/options interface, focusing on paths, appearance, model configurations, and keybindings. This approach prioritizes functionality while modernizing the aesthetic gradually.

thoughts.subject: Outlining the Structure
thoughts.description:
\n\n

My current thinking pivots to project organization. The existing `src/gui` will be restructured using submodules. Specifically, I'll divide it into `components`, for reusable widgets, `tabs`, to manage the main views, and `windows` for secondary interfaces. Then, for the "Label Studio" look, I'll aim for a dashboard, annotation view, and control panel. The central aim is now how to mimic the "flow" of Label Studio for a more intuitive user experience.

thoughts.subject: Executing the Plan
thoughts.description:
\n\n

I've started with the initial steps as outlined, updating `requirements.txt` to include `customtkinter`. I'm creating a `SettingsManager` using a JSON file for persistence, and implementing the `MainDashboard` class. I've also established a base class for new windows to promote reusability. The dashboard, with its card-based project layout, is underway, and I will be working to incorporate the "Label Studio" look-and-feel.

thoughts.subject: Finalizing the Strategy
thoughts.description:
\n\n

I've distilled the core plan. I'm focusing on adopting `customtkinter`, while keeping `tkinter.Canvas` for high-performance drawing. Structuring the project with submodules is essential for maintainability. The main approach centers on a `SettingsManager` and a card-based `MainDashboard` mimicking the Label Studio look. I will need to be careful with the custom widgets, making sure they integrate smoothly. The goal is a modernized feel without a complete code rewrite.

import customtkinter as ctk

class ProjectCard(ctk.CTkFrame):
    """
    A clickable card representing a project.
    """
    def __init__(self, master, project_name, modality, path, on_click_callback, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(master, **kwargs)
        self.project_path = path
        self.callback = on_click_callback
        
        # Style logic
        self.configure(fg_color=("gray85", "gray20")) # Light/Dark
        self.bind("<Button-1>", self._on_click)
        self.bind("<Enter>", self._on_enter)
        self.bind("<Leave>", self._on_leave)

        # Icon/Color Strip based on modality
        modality_color = "#3B8ED0" # Blue Vision
        if modality == "audio": modality_color = "#E04F5F" # Red Audio
        if modality == "video": modality_color = "#2CC985" # Green Video
        
        self.indicator = ctk.CTkFrame(self, width=10, fg_color=modality_color, corner_radius=6)
        self.indicator.pack(side="left", fill="y", padx=(0, 10))
        self.indicator.bind("<Button-1>", self._on_click)

        # Info
        self.info_frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self, fg_color="transparent")
        self.info_frame.pack(side="left", fill="both", expand=True, pady=10)
        
        self.lbl_name = ctk.CTkLabel(self.info_frame, text=project_name, font=("Roboto Medium", 16))
        self.lbl_name.pack(anchor="w")
        self.lbl_name.bind("<Button-1>", self._on_click)
        
        self.lbl_mod = ctk.CTkLabel(self.info_frame, text=modality.upper(), font=("Roboto", 11), text_color="gray60")
        self.lbl_mod.pack(anchor="w")
        self.lbl_mod.bind("<Button-1>", self._on_click)

        # Path (Hidden/Small)
        self.lbl_path = ctk.CTkLabel(self.info_frame, text=path, font=("Roboto", 10), text_color="gray50")
        self.lbl_path.pack(anchor="w", pady=(5,0))
        
        # Action Button (Open)
        self.btn_open = ctk.CTkButton(self, text="Open", width=60, height=24, fg_color=modality_color, command=self._on_click)
        self.btn_open.pack(side="right", padx=15)

    def _on_click(self, event=None):
        if self.callback:
            self.callback(self.project_path)

    def _on_enter(self, event):
        self.configure(border_width=2, border_color=("gray70", "gray40"))

    def _on_leave(self, event):
        self.configure(border_width=0)
